## Los Cardones National Park: giant cacti and Salta's high-altitude road

Los Cardones lies in Salta Province in northwestern [Argentina](/argentina/). Columnar cardón cacti grow on exposed slopes and highland plains, while winding mountain roads climb towards plateaus with expansive views of the Andes.

The park lies along a characteristic driving route from the city of Salta to [Cachi](/argentina/place/cachi/). Visitors therefore often discover it en route, stopping at viewpoints and short nature trails. Driving through the park and exploring its landscapes in depth, however, take different amounts of time.

## Why giant cardón cacti grow here

The cardón is a large columnar cactus adapted to dry conditions and strong sunshine. It grows very slowly, so tall mature specimens are an important and particularly vulnerable feature of the landscape. The park protects more than just cacti: its territory covers several natural environments, from dry valleys and mountain slopes to high-altitude areas.

Watching the vegetation change as the road climbs is part of the experience. Lower down are shrubs and greener slopes; higher up, the country opens into rocky areas and stands of cardón cacti. Animals in these arid landscapes are harder to spot than plants, so sightings of particular species cannot be promised.

## Getting there: Cuesta del Obispo and Recta del Tin Tin

The road west from Salta climbs scenic Cuesta del Obispo towards Piedra del Molino. Elevations along the way exceed 3,000 metres above sea level. The route then crosses a high plateau and the famous straight stretch known as Recta del Tin Tin.

The drive is an attraction in itself: natural zones change along the way, and in clear weather distant mountain panoramas unfold. But road surface and weather conditions require attention. Higher sections can be cold even on sunny days, and clouds or precipitation may seriously reduce visibility.

The park administration gives Provincial Route 33 as an approach and says visits are possible year-round, although **April to November** is often recommended for travel. Check current access hours, restrictions and road conditions before setting out.

## What to see inside the park

Among the accessible attractions are short interpretive trails near Recta del Tin Tin. **Caminos del Pasado**, for example, introduces a historic route, while **Secretos del Cardonal** focuses on the local vegetation and natural environment. Each has designated starting points and visiting rules; do not stop anywhere among the cacti or leave authorised trails.

The panoramas around Piedra del Molino and the high plains are also worth exploring. Decide in advance whether a handful of short stops will be enough or whether you want to follow nature trails. The latter makes the day considerably fuller.

A park visit pairs naturally with the Calchaquí Valleys, [Cachi](/argentina/place/cachi/) and the wine-growing areas around [Cafayate](/argentina/place/cafayate/). A direct journey from Salta to Cafayate does not necessarily pass through Los Cardones, however, so the actual route must be checked against the itinerary.

## Altitude, sun and preparation

One of the most noticeable aspects of the route is the rapid climb from the valley to elevations above 3,000 metres. Even on a brief visit, some people need to be careful about physical exertion. Water, a hat, sunglasses, a warm layer and a windproof jacket are particularly useful.

Avoid rushing into strenuous uphill walks immediately after ascending by vehicle. If you have a medical condition that makes altitude or exertion risky, discuss the trip with your doctor beforehand. An independent hike and a roadside viewpoint may require different levels of preparation.

When choosing [Argentina tours](/argentina/tour/) through the northwest, check the actual stops included. A mention of Salta Province in the title does not guarantee a visit to Los Cardones. The route should either pass through the park or list it explicitly.

## Frequently asked questions about Los Cardones

### Can I see the cacti without a long hike?

Yes. Many of the characteristic landscapes can be seen from the road or along short authorised trails. Choose stops according to the time available, elevation and your fitness.

### How high is the park?

Its territory spans different elevations, and the popular road through Piedra del Molino climbs above 3,000 metres. The altitude depends on where you stop.

### Can I combine Los Cardones and Cachi?

Yes. This is the usual driving route from Salta to Cachi. But allow for more than the distance alone: the mountain ascent, photo stops and trail visits all add to the day's duration.

## Tours through Los Cardones: the high-altitude part of an Argentina journey

[Los Cardones National Park](/argentina/place/los-cardones-national-park/) lies in Salta Province. The road passes among giant cacti, dry mountain slopes and high-altitude plains. You can explore the area while travelling to Cachi, or follow short authorised trails if you have more time.

Our selection features itineraries in which Los Cardones forms part of the main geographical route. They differ in more than the number of days: some explore northwestern Argentina in depth, while others combine Salta with Buenos Aires, Iguazú and other regions.

## Which itinerary should you choose?

### Amazing Salta: focus on the northwest

On the [Amazing Salta tour](/argentina/tour/amazing-salta/), mountain valleys and settlements of the northwest occupy much of the journey. Besides Los Cardones, the itinerary includes the Cafayate wine region, Purmamarca, Quebrada de Humahuaca and Salinas Grandes.

This option suits travellers who value highland landscapes and historic towns more than visiting numerous distant regions in a single holiday. The roads themselves become part of the experience, with elevation, vegetation and the colours of mountain slopes gradually changing.

### Buenos Aires, Salta and Iguazú: three different regions

The [Buenos Aires, Salta and Iguazú journey](/multi-country/tour/buenos-aires-salta-iguazu/) combines the capital's architecture, the arid Andes and the tropical environment around the waterfalls. Los Cardones belongs to the northwest section of the main itinerary, together with Cafayate, Purmamarca and the salt flat.

Choose it if you want to discover several sides of Argentina and are happy to divide your time in each region between travel and excursions.

| Itinerary | Main difference |
|---|---|
| [Amazing Salta](/argentina/tour/amazing-salta/) | Greater focus on Salta Province and neighbouring highland areas |
| [Buenos Aires, Salta and Iguazú](/multi-country/tour/buenos-aires-salta-iguazu/) | The northwest as part of a journey through the capital and the waterfalls |

You will also find other current programmes visiting the park above. The complete itinerary and duration of each journey are available on its own page.

## What is particularly interesting in the park?

The scenery of Los Cardones changes as the road climbs from the valleys. One famous section is the straight high-altitude Recta del Tin Tin road. Nearby are short interpretive trails, including Caminos del Pasado and Secretos del Cardonal. Visiting rules and designated stopping places apply.

The Cuesta del Obispo road offers mountain switchbacks and the Piedra del Molino area. Popular sections rise above 3,000 metres, so warm clothing and sun protection are worth taking even if you are not planning a long hike.

Los Cardones is commonly combined with [Cachi](/argentina/place/cachi/) and other stops on the Salta route. If an itinerary lists several towns, check their order by day: distances and mountain roads do not allow all the sites to be explored equally thoroughly in a brief stop.

## Comparing the conditions of your journey

Start by checking how much time is devoted specifically to Los Cardones and the neighbouring valleys. Driving along a road through the park, walking an accessible trail and spending a dedicated day in the region offer different experiences.

Next, compare overnight stays, transfers, meals and excursions. The actual inclusions depend on the selected tour. Being part of the main route does not automatically mean that every optional stop or activity within the park is covered by the price.

Finally, consider the elevation. After cities and lowlands, the dry mountain air, wind and strong sun feel different. When planning the route, allow sufficient time for transfers and avoid excessive exertion immediately after the ascent.

## Frequently asked questions about tours through Los Cardones

### Can I see the park without challenging trekking?

Yes. Characteristic panoramas, cardón cacti and high mountain road sections are accessible by vehicle. Walks can be added along authorised trails.

### Can Los Cardones and Cachi be visited on the same trip?

Yes. The park lies along the established route from Salta towards Cachi. Allow time for viewpoint stops and walks when planning the day.

### Which tour is best for a first introduction to Salta?

If the northwestern valleys are your priority, compare [Amazing Salta](/argentina/tour/amazing-salta/) with other regional itineraries. For a broader journey around the country, consider [Buenos Aires, Salta and Iguazú](/multi-country/tour/buenos-aires-salta-iguazu/).

## Los Glaciares National Park: Patagonia's glaciers and mountains

Los Glaciares lies in Santa Cruz Province in southern [Argentina](/argentina/). It protects glaciers of the Southern Patagonian Ice Field, mountain ranges and large lakes. The park is inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List for its exceptional natural landscapes.

Los Glaciares has two best-known bases for visitors: [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/) for trips to [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/), and [El Chaltén](/argentina/place/el-chalten/) for hiking routes around Fitz Roy and Cerro Torre. Think of them as two parts of a larger journey, not as neighbouring viewpoints.

## Perito Moreno: a glacier without a difficult hike

Perito Moreno Glacier can be viewed from a network of designated paths and observation platforms. They offer perspectives on the ice front from different heights and distances. For most travellers, this is the principal way to see the glacier: you can select a section suited to your mobility and spend time at the viewpoints.

Sometimes blocks of ice break off the front and fall into the lake. It is a spectacular natural phenomenon, but the timing and frequency of icefalls cannot be predicted. Planning a visit around a specific calving event makes little sense.

Separate boat excursions and specialist trips onto the ice are also available. **Walking on the boardwalks, taking a boat trip and trekking on the glacier are different products.** Ice walking requires organised guiding, specialist equipment and compliance with operator restrictions. Do not assume it is included in a tour simply because Perito Moreno is mentioned.

## El Chaltén: hiking routes around Fitz Roy

The northern part of the park is associated with [El Chaltén](/argentina/place/el-chalten/). Trails lead from here to valleys, lagoons and mountain viewpoints around Fitz Roy and Cerro Torre. Choosing a trail is less about the photographs than its distance, elevation gain and the time actually needed to return.

A short walk to a nearby panorama and a full hike to Laguna de los Tres require different preparation. In the El Chaltén area, registration for certain mountain routes, advance reservations for overnight stays and checks on current trail conditions may be required. The park administration sets the applicable rules.

Strong winds and rapidly changing clouds can obscure mountain views even in the height of summer. For several demanding hikes, an extra day for poor weather is more sensible than relying on one perfect weather window.

## Choosing between the southern and northern sectors

| Base | Main focus |
|---|---|
| El Calafate | Perito Moreno and glacier cruises |
| El Chaltén | Trekking and mountain panoramas |

Visitors travel from El Calafate to the Perito Moreno area by road. There is a separate overland transfer of approximately 200 kilometres between El Calafate and El Chaltén. Seeing the glacier in the morning and completing a major mountain trek in the afternoon is therefore not a realistic single-day itinerary.

For a multi-day visit, first decide what matters most: glacier viewpoints, a boat trip or mountain trails. Then choose the appropriate base and number of nights. Both parts of the park can be combined if the length of your journey allows. Compare [Argentina tours](/argentina/tour/) and [Argentina adventure itineraries](/interests/adventure/tours/argentina/) by their actual day-by-day programmes.

## Weather, access and visiting rules

Los Glaciares offers different activities throughout the year, but practical conditions change considerably. Many hiking routes are accessible in warmer months, although wind, precipitation and cold remain possible. In winter, some roads and trails may be covered in snow and ice. A summer plan for independent trekking should not simply be transferred to a winter visit.

Before departure, check the current admission fee, access hours for your chosen sector, registration requirements and conditions for the particular excursion. There are multiple entrances to the park; a ticket or permit for one activity should not automatically be considered sufficient for every other one.

Stay on designated paths in natural areas. Bring layers of warm clothing, a waterproof jacket, sturdy shoes, water and spare time. Drones and visits with pets are restricted by the protected area's rules.

## Frequently asked questions about Los Glaciares

### Can I see Perito Moreno without trekking?

Yes. The main visit is possible along designated viewing boardwalks, with sections of varying physical difficulty. Stepping directly onto the ice requires a separate specialist excursion.

### Is one day enough for the whole park?

No, not if you want to see both Perito Moreno and the mountain trails around El Chaltén. These areas are far apart and each deserves dedicated time.

### When is the best time for hiking?

For most summer routes, visitors choose the warmer Southern Hemisphere months. However, Patagonian weather is unpredictable, and trail access and park rules must be checked before travelling.

## Tours through Los Glaciares: glaciers and mountains of Argentine Patagonia

[Los Glaciares National Park](/argentina/place/los-glaciares-national-park/) in southern Argentina is famous for Perito Moreno Glacier, its lakes and mountain massifs. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The park extends far beyond a single viewpoint, so trips through it differ in both duration and activities.

Our selection includes itineraries in which the park is a main focus, as well as longer journeys through Patagonia that cross into Chile. The main question when choosing is whether you primarily want to see the glacier, hike mountain trails or combine both.

## Northern and southern sectors: what's the difference?

### El Calafate and Perito Moreno

[El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/) is the principal base for visits to [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/). Its ice wall can be seen from designated viewing boardwalks. Some individual excursions may add a boat trip or a walk directly on the ice, but these are separate activities and should not be assumed to be included on every tour.

A day around Perito Moreno usually involves the journey there, viewing the glacier and time at the observation platforms. The more additional activities you plan, the more carefully the schedule and conditions should be checked.

### El Chaltén and mountain trails

[El Chaltén](/argentina/place/el-chalten/) is associated with the northern part of Los Glaciares, including hiking trails around Fitz Roy. A short walk to a nearby viewpoint and an extended mountain trek require different fitness levels.

If mountain hikes matter more than glacier boardwalks, compare the actual itinerary days and time reserved for poor weather. Transfers between the two bases and the hikes themselves take time; seeing both areas thoroughly is not normally possible in a single day.

## Tours worth comparing

### Luxury Patagonia: Argentina and Chile

The [10-day Luxury Patagonia tour](/multi-country/tour/luxury-patagonia-10-days/) combines Argentina's glacial landscapes with scenery in Chile. El Calafate and other southern areas feature on the route before the journey continues through Patagonia towards Chile.

This option is appealing if you want to experience the natural diversity of the region in one trip, while prioritising an organised sequence of key stops over a multi-day independent hike.

### Argentina, Chile and Patagonia in 13 days

The [13-day Argentina and Chile itinerary](/multi-country/tour/argentina-chile-patagonia-13-days/) combines southern Argentina and its mountain landscapes with the Chilean side of Patagonia. Compared with shorter sightseeing journeys, it allows more opportunities to divide your time between glaciers, mountain areas and transfers.

| Journey | What to consider |
|---|---|
| [Luxury Patagonia, 10 days](/multi-country/tour/luxury-patagonia-10-days/) | A compact combination of glaciers and several regions of Argentina and Chile |
| [Argentina and Chile, 13 days](/multi-country/tour/argentina-chile-patagonia-13-days/) | A longer programme covering diverse natural areas of Patagonia |

You can also choose journeys that combine southern Argentina with other parts of the country. For example, the [journey from glaciers to Iguazú Falls](/multi-country/tour/argentina-glaciers-to-iguazu-falls/) reveals very different landscapes on a single itinerary. When comparing, check the actual days spent in Los Glaciares: a tour's total duration does not equal the time spent in the park.

## Season, physical demands and travel logistics

Weather in southern Patagonia can change rapidly. Strong winds, rain and cloud are possible even in warm months. For trips to the glacier, bring wind and rain protection; for mountain walks, suitable footwear and extra time are important.

Access to the park's different areas, visiting rules, admission and requirements for particular routes can change. Check the conditions for your intended sector with the park administration before travelling. A tour stopping at El Calafate does not, in itself, confirm that glacier trekking or a boat ride is included.

We recommend evaluating each itinerary by its specific days, rather than the number of natural attractions named in its title. This makes it easier to see where there will be time for unhurried walks and where much of the day is spent travelling.

## Frequently asked questions about tours through Los Glaciares

### Can I see Perito Moreno without going onto the ice?

Yes. Viewing boardwalks allow visitors to see the glacier from different angles. Walking on the ice requires a separate organised activity.

### Is it worth combining El Calafate and El Chaltén?

Yes, if the itinerary leaves time for transfers and different activities. Perito Moreno and El Chaltén's mountain trails belong to different parts of this large park.

### How does an Argentina-only tour differ from a journey through Chile?

Crossing into Chile adds different natural regions and border logistics. It may reduce the time available in Los Glaciares itself, however, so compare each itinerary's actual stops and conditions.

## Los Penitentes: a mountain area on the way to Aconcagua

Los Penitentes lies on Argentina's high mountain RN 7 road, leading from [Mendoza](/argentina/place/mendoza/) towards [Aconcagua](/argentina/place/aconcagua/) and the Chilean border. The name has long been associated with a ski resort, but on most sightseeing itineraries the main attraction is the Andes themselves: open valleys, rocky ridges, snow-covered slopes in the colder months and the dramatic change of scenery after Mendoza's vineyards.

Los Penitentes is best understood as a distinct stop along the "high mountain road". Ski holidays and ordinary sightseeing visits, however, have different requirements. The presence of a resort area does not mean that lifts are operating, slopes are open or equipment rental is available on a particular day.

## Where are the Los Penitentes mountains?

According to the Mendoza provincial government, the area is approximately 170 kilometres from Mendoza city along RN 7, in the Las Heras department. The road passes through mountain valleys, gradually climbing into harsher parts of the Andes. Itineraries often include [Uspallata](/argentina/place/uspallata/), [Puente del Inca](/argentina/place/puente-del-inca/), [Aconcagua](/argentina/place/aconcagua/) and [Las Cuevas](/argentina/place/las-cuevas/).

Distance from the city is not the only consideration. Winding mountain roads, roadworks, weather restrictions and several stops can take up most of the day. On a sightseeing excursion, decide in advance where you want the longest stop: the natural bridge, Aconcagua panoramas or the Los Penitentes mountain complex itself.

## What is there to see outside ski season?

Without snow, Los Penitentes remains a striking mountain landscape. Dry sections of the valley accentuate the rocky ridgelines, while resort facilities illustrate how people use the high mountains for seasonal recreation.

On road excursions, visitors stop here for mountain views and photographs. That may be enough to appreciate the contrast between lower Mendoza and the central Andes. A full trek requires a separately chosen route and conditions; a brief stop at the mountain centre is not the same as setting out on a mountain trail.

For short walks, use confirmed public areas. Avoid closed barriers, operational zones and slopes showing signs of avalanche danger.

## Los Penitentes in winter: snow and seasonal activities

The area is historically associated with winter sports. In different seasons, local authorities have described skiing, snow activities and walks with snow-covered slopes as the backdrop. But the exact range of activities depends on snowfall, safety, resort operations and decisions by local providers. The place name alone is no grounds for promising that skiing will be available.

For travellers, this means two different possibilities:

| Purpose | What to check |
|---|---|
| See snow | Weather and road access |
| Ski | Lift and slope operations, available services |
| Sightseeing drive | Stops and return time |

Conditions change even within winter. There may be less snow than expected, and heavy snowfall can sometimes close the road. Current official road notices and the chosen operator's announcements are more useful than last year's itinerary.

## Combining Los Penitentes with Aconcagua and Puente del Inca

The most natural connection is the high-altitude route from [Mendoza](/argentina/place/mendoza/). Beyond the lower valleys are [Uspallata](/argentina/place/uspallata/), stretches with views of the Los Penitentes slopes and the [Puente del Inca](/argentina/place/puente-del-inca/) area. If you plan to visit [Aconcagua](/argentina/place/aconcagua/), establish in advance which parts of the protected area are open and whether your intended activity requires a separate permit.

Each stop has a different appeal. Los Penitentes introduces seasonal life in the high mountains and rocky slopes; Puente del Inca is known for its natural mineral arch; Aconcagua is the continent's highest peak, within a protected area subject to specific access rules. The inclusion of all three names on an itinerary does not guarantee lengthy walks at each.

Farther towards the border lies [Las Cuevas](/argentina/place/las-cuevas/). Continuing depends on conditions on RN 7; a sightseeing excursion should not be confused with a border crossing and full trip into Chile.

## Practical preparation for a high mountain day

Mountain temperatures, wind and sunlight can differ sharply from conditions in town. Layering clothing is helpful: closed shoes, a warm jacket, sun protection and water are useful during short stops. Snow activities require additional equipment determined by the specific activity.

Altitude can affect how you feel, especially after a rapid ascent by vehicle. Avoid overexertion immediately upon arrival, consider any medical restrictions and discuss them in advance when arranging the journey.

If part of the road is closed, do not independently rearrange the route. Rely on local official notices and actual access to each intended section instead. When comparing [Argentina tours](/argentina/tour/), examine the specific stops and length of the mountain days, rather than a general promise to "see the Andes".

## Frequently asked questions about Los Penitentes

### Is Los Penitentes a ski resort?

It has a history as a ski complex, but the operating status of lifts and winter services changes by season. Check the current operator's announcements before planning to ski.

### Can I visit in summer?

Yes. The area remains part of the high mountain route to [Aconcagua](/argentina/place/aconcagua/) and [Puente del Inca](/argentina/place/puente-del-inca/). Summer visits generally focus on mountain scenery rather than winter activities.

### How far is it from Mendoza?

Los Penitentes is about 170 kilometres from the city. Actual travel time depends on road conditions, weather and stops along the way.

### Is trekking essential?

No. A sightseeing stop at an accessible area is enough for an introduction to the landscape. A full walking route requires separate planning and assessment of its difficulty.
